sequences.mechanism: Bile production, modification, storage and meal-associated release are different processes. The gallbladder stores liver-produced bile; its mucosa concentrates it.

steps.title: Liver produces bile
steps.explanation: Hepatocytes actively secrete bile constituents into canaliculi; osmotic water movement contributes to bile formation. Canaliculi and canals of Hering are unmodeled here; the named hepatic ducts show the gross exit.

steps.title: Ducts modify and carry bile
steps.explanation: Cholangiocytes add bicarbonate-rich fluid, with secretin-responsive transport. Duct epithelium and its transporters are explained in text rather than added to this gross specimen.

steps.title: Gallbladder stores and concentrates
steps.explanation: Between meals, downstream resistance favors entry through the cystic duct into the gallbladder. Water and electrolyte absorption concentrates stored bile. This is a predominant storage state, not a claim of zero duodenal flow or a tightly shut valve.

steps.title: Meal-associated bile release
steps.explanation: Nutrients stimulate CCK-related regulation: gallbladder smooth muscle contracts and sphincter resistance falls. Bile exits through the same cystic duct toward the common bile duct, ampulla and major papilla into D2. The cystic duct has bidirectional use across states.

steps.title: Inspect the route through the papilla
steps.explanation: Hide the sphincter selector only to expose the outlet. This visibility action does not depict relaxation. The shared ampullary arrangement is representative and variable in individuals; the intentional D2 specimen window differs from the actual papillary opening.

schematic_limitations: No gallbladder volume change, sphincter deformation, pressure field or flow velocity is implemented.
Canalicular secretion, duct transporters and epithelial absorption are explanatory text, not microscopic geometry.
Do not imply all hepatic bile must visit the gallbladder before entering the duodenum.
Fasting and fed states overlap and have cyclic activity; the steps are teaching states, not measured time intervals.

sequences.mechanism: Acinar tissue provides digestive enzymes; ductal tissue supplies bicarbonate-rich aqueous secretion that transports enzymes and helps neutralize gastric acid.

steps.title: Acid enters the proximal duodenum
steps.explanation: Acidic chyme stimulates duodenal S cells to release secretin into blood. Secretin acts on pancreatic ductal cells; cholinergic inputs contribute. S cells and hormone travel are unmodeled.

native_view.note: Acidic chyme stimulates duodenal S cells to release secretin into blood. Secretin acts on pancreatic ductal cells; cholinergic inputs contribute. S cells and hormone travel are unmodeled.

steps.title: Ductal bicarbonate and water
steps.explanation: Secretin signaling raises duct-cell cAMP; CFTR-associated apical anion transport and chloride/bicarbonate exchange support bicarbonate secretion. Sodium and water follow electrical/osmotic gradients. Ductular secretion carries acinar products toward the intestine.

steps.title: Nutrients increase enzyme secretion
steps.explanation: Fat and protein digestion products stimulate intestinal CCK-related hormonal and vagovagal pathways. Acinar cells have basal rough ER and apical secretory granules; the gross head/body/tail selectors are context, not separate secretion compartments.

steps.title: Two secretory functions share ductal delivery
steps.explanation: Duct fluid transports digestive enzymes to the duodenum. Bicarbonate helps provide a suitable pH for their activity. The accessory duct and minor papilla remain separately identifiable; this specimen does not establish individual duct configuration.

schematic_limitations: No acini, centroacinar cells, S cells, I cells or molecular transporters are geometric parts of this gross model.
No enzyme activation kinetics, exocytosis morphs or hormone particle trajectories are claimed.
Bicarbonate/anion transport is summarized; transporter contributions and their relative dominance are not quantified.
Pancreatic secretions are not absent during fasting. Endocrine insulin/glucagon release uses blood rather than these exocrine ducts and is outside this sequence.

sequences.mechanism: Portal and arterial blood enter liver microcirculation through separate gross routes; mixed sinusoidal blood ultimately leaves through hepatic veins into the IVC.

steps.title: Portal inflow from abdominal organs
steps.explanation: Trace superior mesenteric and splenic contributions toward the hepatic portal vein, posterior to the pancreatic neck. The inferior mesenteric tributary retains its depicted insertion. This portal blood brings absorbed substances to the liver; it is not oxygen-free.

steps.title: Hepatic arterial supply
steps.explanation: Follow the abdominal aorta, coeliac trunk, common hepatic artery and hepatic artery proper to right and left hepatic arteries. These provide the second, more oxygenated inflow. The schematic calibres do not encode relative blood-flow fractions.

steps.title: Hepatic venous drainage
steps.explanation: Central venous drainage converges into hepatic veins and then the IVC. Compare this exit with portal entry. The named hepatic-veins selector represents the drainage network; vessel crossings must not be taught as junctions.

sequences.mechanism: At the liver, biliary outflow and vascular inflow are different systems that run together locally without sharing a lumen.

steps.title: Three neighboring routes at the porta
steps.explanation: Compare hepatic portal vein and hepatic arterial entry with right/left hepatic duct exit. Proximity does not mean luminal communication; these selectors preserve independent passage systems.

native_view.note: Compare hepatic portal vein and hepatic arterial entry with right/left hepatic duct exit. Proximity does not mean luminal communication; these selectors preserve independent passage systems.

steps.title: Microscopic directions differ
steps.explanation: In lobular teaching, blood passes from portal-region inflow toward central venous outflow; bile produced by hepatocytes drains toward portal-region ducts. This model shows gross trunks only. Open the separately reviewed liver-lobule model for microscopic orientation; do not map its scale onto this specimen.

schematic_limitations: There is no direct blood-to-bile connection. Secretion across hepatocyte membranes is explained, not simulated.

sequences.mechanism: Bile-acid reuse links a luminal digestive route to portal venous return, with an unmodeled intestinal absorption step.

steps.title: Bile supports lipid digestion and absorption
steps.explanation: Bile salts disperse lipids and help solubilize digestion products. They do not replace pancreatic digestive enzymes. Follow delivery through the major papilla into the proximal intestinal lumen.

steps.title: Ileal reabsorption and portal return
steps.explanation: Most bile acids are reabsorbed distally in the ileum and return through portal blood for hepatic uptake and resecretion. The ileum and its absorption machinery are absent. This transition is text-only; the shown jejunal cut end is not the ileal absorption site.
